spendPerDayCents.description: Most model spend across a day, in US cents

spendPerRunCents.description: Most model spend one run may make, in US cents

writesPerDay.description: Most writes it may make on its own in a day

Change.description: One proposed change to an agent: what it targets, the new value, and the reason and evidence for it

duty.description: The duty to add when target is "add-duty"; null otherwise

evidence.description: The counts from the record that support the change, as the model cited them

from.description: The current value, as the model stated it; not checked against the agent, and null when the model gave none

target.description: What the change touches: "job", "routing", "persona", "duty:<name>:text", "duty:<name>:every" (an existing duty), or "add-duty" (with duty)

to.description: The new value: text for job, routing, persona and duty text, a six-field cron for a duty's cadence; ignored for add-duty

why.description: The model's reason for the change

ChatCompletion.description: An agent's answer in OpenAI's chat.completion shape, answered by the chat completions endpoints when stream is not true

choices.description: Exactly one choice, holding the agent's answer

created.description: When the turn started, in Unix epoch seconds

embabel.description: What the turn did; present only when the request set embabel_evidence

id.description: chatcmpl- followed by a random UUID, new for every completion

model.description: Name of the agent that answered, or world

ChatCompletionRequest.description: An OpenAI chat completion request to an agent, sent to POST /openai/v1/chat/completions or /agents/{name}/v1/chat/completions. Fields OpenAI defines and this does not list (tools, top_p…) are ignored; the embabel_ fields are this server's own.

embabel_conversation.description: Conversation name the caller chooses: the same name, from any client, continues the same conversation with this agent. Absent or blank, the conversation is recognised from the user and how the history began.

embabel_evidence.description: True adds the embabel evidence object to the response (on the final chunk when streaming); otherwise it is absent

embabel_observing.description: True refuses every effect the agent attempts this turn, even if it is on duty, and reports what it would have done

embabel_realms.description: Realm names to narrow the conversation to, from among the agent's own; never adds one. Absent or empty keeps all of them.

embabel_verbosity.description: Reply length: terse asks for a sentence or two, full for a full answer, normal (or absent, or any other value) for neither. Case-insensitive.

max_completion_tokens.description: Reply length cap in tokens, preferred over max_tokens; capped at the agent's declared most, ignored when it declares none

max_tokens.description: Reply length cap in tokens, used when max_completion_tokens is absent; capped at the agent's declared most, ignored when it declares none

messages.description: The conversation so far, oldest first, as OpenAI clients resend it each time. The newest user message is the turn answered; earlier user and assistant messages are context. At least one non-blank user message is required.

model.description: Name of the agent to talk to, as listed by GET /openai/v1/models, or world for the world itself; ignored on an agent's own base URL, where the path names the agent

stream.description: True answers as server-sent chat.completion.chunk events ending in [DONE]; the whole answer arrives as one content chunk. Absent or false answers one chat.completion.

temperature.description: Sampling temperature, clamped into the range the agent declares; ignored when the agent declares none

user.description: The client's own end-user id, when it sends one; part of how a conversation is recognised, so two of its users' chats stay apart

Choice.description: One answer in a chat completion; there is only ever one

ConsolePreferenceEntry.description: One console setting and when it was set

at.description: When the change was made, epoch milliseconds. A write older than the stored entry is ignored; a time ahead of the server's clock is taken as now

value.description: The setting's value as the console wrote it, any JSON; null removes the setting

ConsolePreferences.description: The acting user's console preferences in their active world: theme, wallpaper, window layout, dock pins and the like, keyed by setting

entries.description: Each setting by key. An entry whose value is null was removed, and is kept so an older write cannot bring it back

updatedAt.description: When a write last changed something, by the server's clock; null when nothing has been stored

version.description: Increases by one on every write that changed something; 0 when nothing has been stored

ConsolePreferencesChange.description: Settings to change, each with the time it was changed; settings not named are left as they are

entries.description: The settings to change, by key. A key is 1-64 letters, digits, '.', '_' or '-', starting with a letter or digit

Counts.description: What the agent has done lately, summed over its record in the units a budget is set in

requestsToday.description: Requests it raised today for a person to approve, from the same midnight

runsLastHour.description: Runs started in the last hour, skipped firings excluded, counted over its 500 most recent runs

writesToday.description: Changes it made today: receipts where a call acted, plus requests a person approved. Today starts at midnight in the user's time zone, UTC when they have none

DataContractBindingSpec.description: A view's version-pinned reference to one object in an ODCS data contract the world holds: a view's `dataContract`

id.description: Id of the ODCS contract; must not be blank

mode.description: `observe` (the default): rows are returned and the verdict reported beside them. `enforce`: rows are withheld when the verdict is `FAIL` or `UNKNOWN`, and the contract must be `active` or `deprecated` to run at all

object.description: The schema object in the contract the view's rows are checked against, by name or else physical name; must not be blank

version.description: The contract version pinned; must not be blank. Only the contract with exactly this id and version governs the view

DataContractCheck.description: One check made when a view's result was evaluated against its data contract

message.description: What it found, in words, naming rows and fields but never their values; null when there is nothing to say

ruleId.description: The contract's own id for a quality or freshness rule, or an `embabel:` id for a check the runtime makes itself, such as `embabel:schema`, `embabel:binding` or `embabel:status`

scope.description: `invocation` for the schema check, which covers this one result; null for every other check

verdict.description: `PASS`, `WARN`, `FAIL`, or `UNKNOWN` when the check could not be made

DataContractEvaluation.description: Evidence that one named view's result was checked against its pinned data contract: the verdict, each check, and whether the rows were withheld. Carried as `dataContract` on the result of a view bound to a contract

apiVersion.description: The ODCS apiVersion the contract declares, such as `v3.1.0`; `v3.1.0` when the view was refused before it ran

available.description: False when the view could not run under its contract: the pinned contract or its object is missing, or its status forbids it. Then no rows are returned, whatever the mode

checkedAt.description: ISO-8601 instant the result was checked

checks.description: Each check made, in the order it was made

id.description: Id of the governing contract, as the view's binding pins it

object.description: The contract object the rows were checked against, as the binding names it

status.description: The contract's ODCS status, such as `active`, `deprecated` or `retired`; `unavailable` when the pinned contract is not in the world

verdict.description: The worst of the checks: `FAIL` if any failed, else `UNKNOWN` if any could not be made, else `WARN` if any warned, else `PASS`

DispatchedError.description: The body the servlet error dispatch answers for a status raised by an exception rather than written by the endpoint. Every failure except 404, which answers the not-found HTML page

error.description: The status's standard reason phrase, such as Bad Request or Forbidden

status.description: The HTTP status code, repeated from the status line

DutyCheck.description: What one check of an agent's duty found: whether the condition it keeps true holds, since when it has not, and what its repair did. Answered by POST /agents/{name}/duties/{duty}/check

agent.description: Name of the agent that holds the duty

agentVersion.description: The agent's signed version number that governed the check; null when no signed version governs it

duty.description: Name of the duty checked, as the agent declares it

lapsedSince.description: ISO-8601 instant this lapse began: the first check that found violations, carried across later lapsed, neglected and unknown checks. Null when upheld, or unknown with no lapse before it

notes.description: Source warnings that left the rows sound, such as a cost note from a realm's producer

onDemand.description: True when somebody asked for this check, as this endpoint does; false for a check on the duty's own schedule

onFallbacks.description: True when a model the duty's view relies on failed and the result stands on a second read with the agent's fallback models

reason.description: Why the state is unknown: the view errored or was not found, a source warned its rows may be wrong or short, or its models failed with no fallback that worked. Null for every other state

repairFailures.description: How many of those repair runs failed or threw

repaired.description: Violating rows the repair routine was run on, at most 25 per check; 0 when the duty declares no repair or its routine does not exist

state.description: `upheld` (the duty's view returned no rows), `lapsed` (it returned violations), `neglected` (lapsed, and during this lapse a request its repair raised was rejected and none approved), or `unknown` (the view could not be read cleanly; see reason)

violations.description: Rows the duty's view returned, each one a violation; 0 when upheld or unknown

wouldHaveCalled.description: Tools the repair tried to call and was refused, each named once: what it would have changed had the check not run observing

DutyView.description: A duty on an agent's card (AgentView.duties): a condition the agent keeps true, with what its latest check and latest passing test run found

checkedAt.description: When the latest check ran, as an ISO-8601 instant; null when it has not been checked

every.description: Six-field cron cadence it is checked on; null when it is only checked on demand

holds.description: Name of the view or DERIVE label whose rows are the violations

lapsedSince.description: When the current lapse began, as an ISO-8601 instant; null when it is not lapsed or has not been checked

name.description: The duty's name within its agent, as POST /agents/{name}/duties/{duty}/check takes it

reason.description: Why the latest check could not tell, when its state is unknown; otherwise null

stage.description: The stage it runs at (off, observing or on): its own declared stage, else the agent's

state.description: The latest check's state: upheld, lapsed, neglected or unknown; null when it has not been checked

status.description: The latest check in words: "upheld", "lapsed since ...", "neglected: ...", "unknown: <reason>", or "not checked yet"

testedAt.description: When this duty last passed a test run, as an ISO-8601 instant; null when it never has

testedVersion.description: The signed agent version that test run checked; going on duty needs it to be the current one. Null when it was never tested

text.description: The condition in the sponsor's words: an Always or a Never

timezone.description: Zone the cadence is read in, as a zone ID such as Europe/London; null reads it in the user's own zone

violations.description: How many violating rows the latest check found; 0 when it has not been checked

ErrorBody.description: An OpenAI-shaped error body, answered by the OpenAI-compatible endpoints when they refuse a request

ErrorDetail.description: Why an OpenAI-compatible request was refused

code.description: model_not_found when no agent of that name may be talked to now, key_scope when the API key does not reach the agent or the world itself, invalid_request when there is no user message to answer or embabel_observing is asked of the world

message.description: Human-readable reason, e.g. why the agent may not be talked to now

Evidence.description: What a chat completion turn did, sent as the embabel field only when the request set embabel_evidence

conversation.description: Id of the chat session the turn ran in

refused.description: What the Gatekeeper refused the agent this turn, each as tool (why), e.g. observing, never or egress; empty when nothing was refused

requests.description: Requests for a person's approval this turn's run raised, in any status; empty when it raised none

run.description: Id of the agent run the turn went as; every request it raised names it. Absent when the turn ran as no agent.

EvidenceRequest.description: A request for a person's approval raised during a chat completion turn

detail.description: What would happen and why, in the business's words

id.description: Request id, as the approvals surface knows it

status.description: pending, approved, failed, rejected or expired

verb.description: Gateway tool the request would call on approval, e.g. odoo_partnerMessagePost

Expected.description: A duty whose last check found violations and that declares a repair: the next check will raise its requests again if nothing changes

Fill.description: A fill: a slow, resumable materialization of one query, re-run a budgeted chunk per tick until a pass buys nothing. What `/admin/kg/fills` starts and lists.

budgetPerTick.description: Units of paid work one tick may buy — a producer fetch group or a group of an inline model judgement, not HTTP requests or tokens. Clamped to 1–500; defaults to 60.

cypher.description: The Cypher every tick re-runs, as it was submitted.

id.description: The fill's id, `fill_` plus 12 hex characters — what `DELETE /admin/kg/fills/{id}` takes.

label.description: A display name for the fill. Empty when none was given.

progress.description: How far the fill has got, as of its most recent tick.

routine.description: The routine the fill runs as, whose agent governs every chunk. Null for a fill an operator started outside any routine run.

userId.description: The id of the user the fill belongs to and runs as.

warning.description: Why this fill will keep polling rather than reach DONE — its producers' records do not outlive a sweep. Decided at start. Null when it can converge, or when the query could not be planned to say.

FillProgress.description: A fill's progress: its state, its tick and paid-call counts, and how much of the sweep is answered.

coverage.description: Keys the producer caches answer, of the total the last pass enumerated. `keysTotal` is null where the query has no denominator; never derive a fraction then.

createdAt.description: Epoch milliseconds at which the fill was started.

lastError.description: Why the most recent tick failed or was refused. Null when it ran clean. An error leaves the fill RUNNING.

lastTickAt.description: Epoch milliseconds of the most recent tick, refused ones included. Null before the first.

liveCallsLastTick.description: Paid calls in the most recent tick alone, counted as `liveCallsTotal` counts them.

liveCallsTotal.description: Paid calls across every tick: producer fetches, in-query model calls and semantic searches.

state.description: RUNNING, DONE (a full pass needed no paid work) or CANCELLED.

ticks.description: Chunks run so far. A chunk refused before it ran — a halt, a ceiling — does not count.

Firing.description: One of an agent's scheduled jobs, a duty check or a routine, with when it next fires

cron.description: The job's six-field cron expression, seconds first

job.description: Name of the scheduler's job: the `job` to send to skip or run-now

nextAt.description: ISO-8601 instant of its next firing; null when the cron does not parse or its zone cannot be read

postponedTo.description: When the skipped firing was postponed rather than dropped, the ISO-8601 instant it runs instead; null otherwise

skipped.description: True when a person has marked the next firing to be skipped

work.description: Name of the duty or routine the job runs

zone.description: IANA zone id the cron is read in: the job's own when it declares one, else the user's (UTC when they have none)

HandlerAvailable.description: A realm-shipped handler available to adopt, which this user has not enabled.

name.description: The realm handler's name, to pass to set-enabled to adopt it.

signalType.description: The signal type that fires it once adopted; '*' = none.

HandlerDryRunRequest.description: A handler body to run observe-only, and what to run it against.

sample.description: A sample signal to bind INSTEAD of sampling the graph — for an event not yet received.

signalType.description: The signal type to sample a real recent event from. Null or '*' means a cron tick.

source.description: The TypeScript handler body to run. Nothing is saved, and the run applies no external effects.

HandlerDryRunResponse.description: The outcome of an observe-only handler run: what it saw, what it logged, and how it ended.

error.description: The failure message when the body threw. Serialized as null otherwise — consumers test for the key.

ok.description: False when the body threw; `error` then carries the message.

output.description: What the body RETURNED, when it returned something. A handler that ends with `return rows` and never logs is not silent — this is its result. Absent when the body returned nothing.

ranAgainst.description: The signal the run actually bound, which may differ from the one asked for.

stdout.description: Everything the body logged. The brief tells a handler to log every effect, so this IS the feedback surface.

HandlerEnabledResponse.description: Acknowledgement of an enable/disable, echoing the state now in force.

enabled.description: The firing state the request set, echoed back.

name.description: The handler the request named.

ok.description: Always true. It does not confirm that a handler of that name exists.

HandlerErrorResponse.description: A refusal carrying only a human-readable reason.

error.description: What went wrong, in the terms the caller can act on.

HandlerGenerateRequest.description: An English description of a handler, optionally as a change to existing source.

current.description: When present, `english` is a CHANGE to this source — the round-trip an editor's Refine drives.

english.description: What the handler should do, in English; with `current`, the change to make to that source.

skills.description: Skills to bundle. They are handed to the writing model as references — prompt contribution AND tools — so a realm's documented idioms are followed rather than re-derived.

HandlerGenerateResponse.description: Generated (or refined) handler source, with the tsc verdict on it.

attempts.description: 1, or 2 when the model was handed its own type errors to fix.

durationMs.description: Server-side time the generation took, attempts included, in milliseconds.

source.description: The generated TypeScript handler body. Nothing is saved.

valid.description: Whether `source` passes the same tsc gate save enforces.

violations.description: The compiler's errors, in the SOURCE's own line coordinates. Empty when `valid`.

HandlerListResponse.description: The handlers this user has, and the realm-shipped ones they could adopt.

available.description: Realm-shipped handlers that are not active for this user, to adopt.

yours.description: Handlers authored in this user's world, sorted by name. Realm-shipped handlers are never listed here.

HandlerListing.description: A handler belonging to this user, with its triggers and whether it is live.

active.description: Whether it currently fires. A saved handler that is off changes nothing.

autonomous.description: When true it may apply external/write effects; when false it runs observe-only.

inputTypeNames.description: Domain types it consumes; empty means reaction-only (dispatcher, never planner).

name.description: The handler's name, as open, save and the other operations take it.

schedule.description: Its 6-field cron expression, or null when not scheduled.

signalType.description: The signal type that fires it; '*' = none.

HandlerMutationResponse.description: Whether the mutation landed, and what the server has to say about it.

message.description: The server's own sentence about the outcome; on a failed save, the TypeScript errors. Show it rather than replace it.

ok.description: Whether the save or delete landed. A save that does not type-check is not persisted.

HandlerOpenResponse.description: One handler's source and metadata, for round-tripping open → edit → save.

autonomous.description: When true it may apply external/write effects; when false it runs observe-only.

description.description: One line describing what it does; the name when it was saved without one.

inputTypeNames.description: Domain types it consumes; empty means reaction-only.

name.description: The name to send back to save, which updates this handler in place.

schedule.description: The 6-field cron expression saved with the handler, or null. A per-user schedule set through set-schedule is not reflected here; list reports it.

signalType.description: `Signal.typeName` (or simple name) that fires it; '*' = none.

skills.description: Skills bundled with it, round-tripped so an edit does not drop them.

source.description: The TypeScript handler body, to edit and send back to save.

HandlerRanAgainst.description: The signal a dry run bound, as sampled — not as requested.

signalId.description: Id of the signal bound: the sampled signal's id, a sample's `id` (else `sample`), or `cron` for a cron tick.

signalType.description: Simple type name of the signal bound: the sampled signal's, or for a sample its `typeName` (else the requested type, else `SampleSignal`), or `CronTick` when nothing matching was on record.

HandlerSaveRequest.description: A handler to create or update, with its triggers.

autonomous.description: When true the handler may apply external/write effects; when false, the default, it runs observe-only.

description.description: One line describing what it does. Defaults to the name.

inputTypeNames.description: Domain types this action consumes. Declaring them makes it planner-chainable rather than reaction-only.

name.description: The handler's name. Saving under an existing name replaces that handler.

outputTypeName.description: Domain type the body returns, bound on the blackboard so later actions chain on it. 'void' for a side-effecting action.

schedule.description: Optional 6-field cron expression; null = not scheduled.

signalType.description: `Signal.typeName` (or simple name) that fires this handler; '*' = none.

skills.description: Skills bundled with this agent, put in front of the model that writes and refines it.

source.description: The TypeScript handler body. Type-checked first: a body that does not compile is not saved.

HandlerScheduleResponse.description: Acknowledgement of a schedule change, echoing the schedule now in force.

name.description: The handler the request named.

ok.description: Always true. It does not confirm that a handler of that name exists.

schedule.description: The cron expression now in force, or null when the schedule was cleared.

HandlerValidateRequest.description: A handler body to type-check without saving or running it.

source.description: The TypeScript handler body to type-check.

HandlerValidateResponse.description: The tsc verdict on a handler body, without saving or running it.

durationMs.description: Server-side time the type-check took, in milliseconds.

valid.description: Whether the body passes the tsc gate save enforces.

violations.description: The compiler's errors, in the SOURCE's own line coordinates. Empty when `valid`.

Hint.description: One tip for a UI to show, from the installation, the world's config or an installed realm. Returned by the `/hints` endpoints.

action.description: A one-click follow-up that fills the host surface's chat input. Null when the tip has none

body.description: The tip itself, as Markdown. Empty when its file gives none

category.description: Grouping the tip belongs to; the stock set uses `hint`, `did-you-know` and `fun-fact`, and a file that names none gets `hint`

icon.description: Icon name as the hint file gives it, passed through uninterpreted. Null when the file gives none

id.description: Identifier built from the hint file's name and the tip's position in it: stable while the file is unchanged, unique across files. What `GET /hints/random` takes in `exclude`

realm.description: Name of the realm that shipped the tip. Null for a tip from the installation or the world's own config

surface.description: Which UI the tip is for: `me` (the chat surfaces), `console` (the worlds console) or `all`

title.description: Short heading for the tip. Empty when its file gives none

HintAction.description: A hint's one-click follow-up: text placed in the host surface's chat input, ready to edit before sending.

chatInput.description: Text to put in the chat input, not sent automatically. Empty when the hint file gives none

label.description: Button text for the follow-up; `Do It` when the hint file gives none

InFlight.description: A run of the agent's still in progress

deadline.description: ISO-8601 instant 30 minutes after it started; a run still open past it is closed as timed out

runId.description: Id of the run, as in GET /agents/{name}/runs/{id}

work.description: The routine, duty or conversation it is running, as its run records it

JsonRpcError.description: The error object of a JSON-RPC response; the A2A card endpoints also answer a refusal with it as the whole body.

code.description: JSON-RPC or A2A error code: -32600 invalid request (also an agent that cannot be talked to now, or that this key may not reach), -32601 method not found, -32602 invalid params, -32603 internal error, -32001 task not found, -32002 task not cancelable, -32003 push notifications not supported, -32004 unsupported operation

message.description: What went wrong, in words for a person to read

JsonRpcRequest.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 call to one agent, the body of POST /agents/{name}/a2a.

id.description: The caller's id for this call, echoed in the response; a string or a number

jsonrpc.description: JSON-RPC version; send `2.0`. The value is not checked

method.description: The A2A method: `message/send`, `tasks/get` or `tasks/cancel`. Streaming and push-notification methods answer an unsupported-operation error, any other a method-not-found error

params.description: The method's params, as the A2A protocol defines them

JsonRpcResponse.description: A JSON-RPC 2.0 response from POST /agents/{name}/a2a, carrying a result or an error, never both.

error.description: On failure, the error; absent on success

id.description: The id of the call this answers, echoed as sent; null when the call carried none

result.description: On success, what the method returned: an A2A Message or Task. Absent on an error

KeyCoverage.description: How much of one execution's key demand was resolved: keysResolved of keysTotal, where a null total means unknown, never zero. Carried as coverage on a fill's progress.

keysResolved.description: Distinct key units, one per producer, key and period, answered in the execution from a cache tier or a successful fetch

keysTotal.description: Distinct key units the execution demanded; null when the sweep has no denominator (totality UNKNOWN), which never means zero

KgAnnotationDiff.description: One proposed property change, as it would be written.

after.description: The value the write would set. Null means the write clears the property.

before.description: The value before the write, or null when the property is new.

identity.description: The target's identity property value. Type depends on the label's identity property.

property.description: The property the write sets; the plan's allowlisted property, the same on every diff.

KgAnnotationDryRunResponse.description: A frozen annotation plan: what WOULD be written, with nothing written yet.

diffs.description: One proposed change per selected node, as it would be written.

expiresAt.description: When the frozen plan lapses, ISO-8601. Echo it back verbatim.

label.description: The node label the statement targets; annotation writes must be allowed on it in the world's annotatable declarations.

planId.description: Pass this to /apply or /undo. Single-use and time-limited.

property.description: The allowlisted property the statement SETs on each selected node.

selected.description: How many nodes the statement selected.

KgAnnotationOutcomeResponse.description: The result of applying or undoing a frozen plan.

applied.description: Targets written: set to the planned value on apply, restored to their prior value on undo.

conflicted.description: Targets that still exist but moved since the plan froze. Skipped, not forced.

disappearedOrUnauthorized.description: Targets that could not be re-bound in scope: deleted, re-owned or re-labeled. Deliberately ONE bucket — separating them would leak whether another tenant's data exists.

planId.description: The plan applied or undone, echoed from the path.

postImages.description: One committed post-image per target written.

selected.description: Targets considered: the frozen plan's selection on apply, the plan's audited writes on undo. applied, conflicted and disappearedOrUnauthorized add up to it.

KgAnnotationPostImage.description: One committed post-image, read back inside the write transaction.

auditId.description: Audit record id for this individual write.

identity.description: The written node's identity property value. Type depends on the label's identity property.

value.description: The property's value as committed, read back after the write; null when the write cleared it.

KgAnswerAccepted.description: Acknowledgement that a parked run accepted the owner's choice.

choice.description: The choice exactly as the request sent it.

runId.description: The run id from the path, echoed back.

state.description: The state the run moved to as a result.

KgAnswerRequest.description: The owner's answer to a run parked awaiting input, sent to `/runs/{runId}/answer`.

choice.description: One of the options the parked run's question offers — for a cost-gate question `proceed`, `narrow`, `background` or `cancel`. Matched trimmed and case-insensitively.

KgAskExposure.description: What the models behind one knowledge-graph ask were shown: the schema groups the question resolved to, and the measured size of the generation and view-selection prompts. Carried as `exposure` on an `/ask` answer.

generationPromptChars.description: Characters in the Cypher-generation prompt. Absent when no query was generated.

groups.description: The schema groups rendered in full for generation, and whose views view selection was offered.

indexed.description: Groups named to the generator by one index line only — no labels, properties or examples.

matched.description: Each named group -> the words that named it, tier first: name:, label:, weak: or keyword:.

resolvedBy.description: How the groups were chosen: WHOLE (nothing to narrow), SCOPE, QUESTION, UNRESOLVED or SELECTOR.

spineOnly.description: True when the always-on core was cut to the spine anchors (the user, Person, Organization).

viewSelectPromptChars.description: Characters in the view-selection prompt. Absent when no view selection ran.

viewsOffered.description: Saved views offered to view selection, of `viewsInWorld`.

KgAskRequest.description: A natural-language question: the body of `/ask`, and of the studio's `/generate`.

question.description: The question in plain language. Cypher is written for it and, on `/ask`, run scoped to the acting user.

KgAskScopeInfo.description: A named scope: a declared realm set an ask can be narrowed to via `scope=`.

description.description: What the scope is for, as its focus declares it. Empty when the declaration gives none.

name.description: The scope's name — the value `scope=` accepts.

realms.description: The realm names whose schema the scoped ask sees (plus the always-on core).

KgBackgroundHandle.description: A handle to a run started in the background.

choices.description: The question a parked run poses to its owner. Absent while running.

state.description: RUNNING, or WAITING_INPUT when the run parked on `choices`.

KgBadChoiceResponse.description: A rejected run answer, listing the choices this endpoint accepts.

error.description: Names the choice that was refused.

KgBadRealmsResponse.description: The scope named realms that are not installed; the installed ones travel with the refusal.

error.description: Names the realms that are not installed.

installed.description: The realm names actually installed in this world.

unknown.description: The requested realm names no installed realm answers to.

KgContractColumn.description: One drafted column, and whether its entry was read or inferred.

evidence.description: `declared` (read from the view) or `sampled` (inferred from rows).

logicalType.description: ODCS logical type, present only when a sample agreed unanimously.

name.description: The column's name, as the view's RETURN aliases it.

suggestions.description: What the sample SUGGESTS but does not prove, as ODCS extension keys.

KgContractDisposition.description: What the server actually did, separate from what it drafted.

bound.description: Whether the view now pins this contract in `observe` mode.

notes.description: Human-readable notes: what was not done, and why.

sampleRows.description: Rows read while sampling. Zero when the view was not run.

sampleTruncated.description: Whether sampling stopped at its row cap.

savedAs.description: World-relative path written, or null when this was a preview.

KgContractRefusal.description: A refusal to draft a contract, naming what about the view made it impossible.

error.description: Why no contract was drafted: no such view, a projection that cannot be read (`*`, a bare variable, an unaliased or duplicate column), or a write the world refused.

KgCreateScopeRequest.description: A named scope to declare: a world-tier focus the ask surface can be narrowed to.

description.description: A line on what the scope is for, written into the focus declaration. Defaults to empty.

name.description: Slug, `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*` — the value `scope=` will accept. No `+`: unencoded it decodes to a space in a query parameter.

realms.description: Installed realm names whose schema the scope's asks see.

candidates.description: Stale nodes this tick picked up. 0 with an `error` means the decorator is unknown.

decorator.description: The decorator name from the path, echoed back, whether or not it is registered.

error.description: Why the tick could not complete, or null. Always present.

failed.description: Candidates whose decoration threw; they stay unstamped, so a later tick tries them again. Above 0 on a forced run answers 500.

skipped.description: Candidates passed over without decorating: no node could be loaded, no single owning user could be resolved, or the tick was interrupted.

KgDecoratorInfo.description: A registered node decorator and the cadence it runs on.

batchSize.description: Most candidates one tick will process.

name.description: The decorator's stable kebab-case identifier, used in the /admin/kg/decorate/{name} routes and as the prefix of its stamp property.

refreshAfter.description: How stale a node must be before it is a candidate again, or `never`.

stampProperty.description: The property stamped on a node once decorated — how staleness is judged.

targetLabels.description: Labels this decorator considers as candidates.

tickInterval.description: How often the scheduled tick fires, ISO-8601 duration.

decorators.description: Every registered decorator, in registration order.

name.description: The deleted view's name, as given in the path.

KgDerivation.description: One member of a derived label or relationship type, with the firing chain that concluded it

elementId.description: The member node's element id, the key to join query rows to traces (RETURN `elementId(x)`). For a derived relationship, the two endpoints' element ids joined by a NUL character and `->`

props.description: Derived property values as they settled at the fixpoint, by property name (the last write wins)

round.description: Fixpoint round, counting from 1, in which this member was first concluded

rule.description: Position, counting from 1, of the rule that first concluded this member

trace.description: Firings oldest first: each rule's first conclusion of this member, and every later firing that changed its values

KgDeriveDemandWire.description: A materialization demand in an ad-hoc rule set: facts fetched into the query before the rules run, as an installed rule set's `requires:` entry

description.description: Why the rule set needs these facts; empty when omitted

materialize.description: Read-only Cypher, MATCH clauses and one RETURN (`RETURN 1` is enough), run after the query has materialized its anchors to deepen what it fetched, e.g. `MATCH (r:NpmRelease)-[:HAS_DEPENDENCY*1..3]->(:NpmDependency) RETURN 1`. May reference the rule set's declared params

KgDeriveRequest.description: Body of POST /admin/kg/derive: a DERIVE rule set to evaluate for this one query, and the Cypher that reads what it derives. Nothing persists; the world's installed rule sets are evaluated alongside it.

cypher.description: The Cypher query to run with the derived label or relationship type visible like any other

derives.description: The label the rules derive, or the relationship type when the heads are relationship patterns: letters, digits and `_`, starting with a letter

description.description: One-line description of the rule set; empty when omitted

name.description: Qualified name for the rule set, `realm/ruleset` style; validator messages and traces name it. Defaults to `adhoc/` followed by `derives`. An installed rule set of the same name is shadowed for this query

paramSpecs.description: Bind variables the rule set declares, by name, in the view-param vocabulary (type, default, description); referenced as `$name` in rule bodies and demands. A param with no default must be given in params

params.description: Invocation values: keys declared in paramSpecs bind the rule bodies, coerced to their declared types; the whole map also binds the query as ordinary params

requires.description: Materialization demands run before the rules; an unsatisfiable one does not fail the query. Empty when omitted

rules.description: The rules: unordered clauses of one definition, at least one, all concluding `derives` and all of the same kind

KgDeriveResponse.description: Answer of POST /admin/kg/derive: the query result, plus every rule set evaluated for it with its derivations

derived.description: Each rule set evaluated for the query, the ad-hoc one and any installed ones it reached, with members, rounds and why traces

result.description: The Cypher query's result, run over the derived overlay

KgDeriveRuleWire.description: One DERIVE rule in an ad-hoc rule set sent to POST /admin/kg/derive: what it concludes (the head) and when (the body)

derive.description: The head: a Cypher node pattern, or a relationship pattern for a rule set deriving a relationship, whose variable names the body binding that becomes a member, whose label or type is the rule set's `derives`, and whose property map defines derived properties from body-bound expressions, e.g. `(e:Blocked {blockedStake: stake})`

from.description: The body: read-only Cypher that binds the head's variables and has no RETURN. It may match the derived label itself

KgDerivedFiring.description: One firing in a derived member's why trace: which rule concluded it, in which fixpoint round, with what property values

props.description: Derived property values this firing concluded, by property name; empty when the head declares none

round.description: Fixpoint round the rule fired in, counting from 1

rule.description: Position of the rule that fired in the rule set's rules, counting from 1

KgDerivedLabel.description: One rule set evaluated for the query: what it derived, how many rounds the fixpoint took, and each member's why trace

derivations.description: Derived members with their traces, in the order concluded, at most 500

label.description: The label, or relationship type, the rule set derives

members.description: Number of members derived, counted in full even when derivations is truncated

rounds.description: Fixpoint rounds run, including the final round that changed nothing

ruleSet.description: Qualified name of the rule set evaluated

truncated.description: True when derivations was capped at 500; members and rounds still cover everything

KgErrorResponse.description: A refusal carrying only a human-readable reason.

error.description: What went wrong, in the terms the caller can act on.

KgExecuteRequest.description: Cypher to run through the virtual-cypher engine — the body of `/execute`, and of `/validate`, which reads only `cypher`.

args.description: Arguments for `params`. A blank value means not supplied, so the default applies.

captureAs.description: Capture the result set as this named scope; reference it later as (x:`$name`). The statement must RETURN one labelled node variable. Synchronous mode only.

cypher.description: The statement, run verbatim — or, when `params` is given, a view body whose `$name` references are substituted first.

params.description: Declared parameters for the cypher, as a view declares them. Each `$name` is substituted from `args` merged over its default, exactly as when a saved view runs.

KgFillCancelled.description: A cancelled fill: which one, and the state it is now in

id.description: The fill's id, echoed back unchanged

state.description: Always `CANCELLED`. Completed chunks stay cached and nothing is rolled back, so this says the fill stopped rather than that its work was undone

KgGenerateContractRequest.description: How to draft an ODCS contract for a named view, and how far to go with it.

args.description: Arguments for a parameterized view. Used only when sampling.

bind.description: Also pin the view to the new contract in `observe` mode. Requires `persist`.

persist.description: Write the draft into the world. False previews it and writes nothing.

sample.description: Run the view under a row cap to infer types and suggestions. Off by default: generation reads the declaration only unless asked to touch data.

KgGenerateContractResponse.description: A drafted ODCS contract for a named view, in `draft` status and unreviewed.

columns.description: One entry per column the view projects, in the order the draft lists them.

contractId.description: The contract's id: a name-based (version 5) UUID over the world and view, so regenerating for the same view yields the same id.

disposition.description: What was written and bound, and what an author still has to do.

mode.description: `declaration` or `sample` — how much of this draft came from data.

status.description: ODCS status of the generated document. Always `draft`.

version.description: The contract's version: `0.1.0` for every generated draft, pre-1.0 because it is unreviewed.

view.description: The name of the view the contract was drafted for.

yaml.description: The contract document. Review this before promoting anything.

KgGenerateRequest.description: A question to write Cypher for, and whether a saved view that answers it may stand in.

preferViews.description: Consult the saved-view catalogue first (default true): a question a curated view already answers comes back as that view's invocation, with `view` set. False generates regardless.

question.description: The natural-language question to write Cypher for.

KgGenerateResponse.description: Generated cypher and what the engine will do with it, without running it.

attempts.description: How many generate-validate rounds it took.

cypher.description: The Cypher written for the question — or, when `view` is set, that view's invocation. Nothing has been executed.

durationMs.description: Wall-clock milliseconds the call took, view matching or generation plus the explanation.

explain.description: What the engine will do when this runs. Best-effort; never fails the call.

question.description: What the user typed, echoed back: the question, or for `/refine` the instruction.

valid.description: Whether the final attempt passed the strict preflight.

view.description: Present when a saved view already answers the question: `cypher` is then that view's invocation, `attempts` is 0, and nothing was generated. Absent when the Cypher was written for this question.

violations.description: What the strict preflight objected to in the final attempt, one entry per defect.

KgInFlightRun.description: A virtual-cypher run currently executing for the acting user.

runId.description: The run's id — also the SSE queryId. Pass it to `/kill/{runId}`.

startedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds at which the run started.

KgInvokeViewRequest.description: Arguments for invoking a saved view, the body of `/views/{name}/invocation` and `/views/{name}/run`.

args.description: Values by declared parameter name, merged over the view's defaults; empty or absent runs it on its defaults. Keys sent beside `args` instead of inside it are refused with a 400 by `/run`.

KgKillResponse.description: The outcome of a kill request.

killed.description: False when the run had already settled, or was never the caller's.

runId.description: The run id from the path, echoed back.

KgPropertyValuesResponse.description: The legal values of a property, from `/schema/{label}/{property}/values`: the closed set, its size when too wide (`tooMany`), or not enumerable — branch on which.

enumerable.description: False when the source cannot be asked at all — NOT the same as an empty set.

label.description: The node label from the path, echoed back.

property.description: The property name from the path, echoed back.

reason.description: Why the domain cannot be enumerated — no such property, a credential-shaped one, a source that is unavailable or cannot be asked. Null unless `enumerable` is false.

tooMany.description: Present when the domain is WIDER than max — its presence IS the signal.

values.description: The closed set, when it fits within the property's declared max.

KgQueryResult.description: The outcome of a virtual-cypher query: rows, the cypher that produced them, and what it cost.

answerBoundary.description: The rows are supporting context only, not a match for the original question.

apiCallLog.description: The actual calls as `producer(keys)`, in order — fan-out is visible here.

apiCalls.description: External fetches the executor made. 0 means everything was cached or local.

capturedScope.description: The scope this result set froze into — present only on a capturing execute.

columnSources.description: Each column -> the expression that computed it, traced back through WITH and UNWIND, e.g. {"total": "sum(b.amount)"}; an unwound column reads "UNWIND <list>". Where the origin cannot be traced with certainty, the column's own RETURN expression is given unchanged. A column name is the query's label for a value, not evidence of what it is.

cypher.description: The cypher that actually ran, after scope rewriting.

dataContract.description: The pinned ODCS identity and invocation verdict, for a contracted named view only.

durationMs.description: Total: bridge-resolve plus materialize plus read.

error.description: Why the query failed, or null when it did not.

exposure.description: What the models behind an `/ask` answer were shown: resolved schema groups and prompt sizes.

fetchedRecords.description: Source records fetched before query-side filtering, cache-served included. Absent when none.

hint.description: What to try instead. Accompanies an empty result only.

llmCallLog.description: The actual LLM calls (kg-ask and agg-*), in order.

llmCalls.description: LLM calls: the generation plus any aggregate reductions. Reasoning only — a semantic anchor's embedding is on `semanticCalls`.

materializedNodes.description: Graph nodes materialized from fetched records in this execution. Absent when none.

question.description: The question asked, echoed back. Present only for `/ask`.

reason.description: Typed outcome when this was not a clean answer — UNBOUNDED, NOT_IN_GRAPH, MISSING_ATTRIBUTE, FETCHED_NOT_MATCHED, PARTIAL_NOT_MATCHED, UNPUSHED_FILTER, DISCONNECTED or INTERNAL_ERROR. May accompany rows when a source failed, a read was refused, or a filter was not applied; absent on a clean answer, including a genuine zero.

rows.description: One map per row, keyed by RETURN column. Empty and meaningless while `run` is present — the run has not finished, which is not the same as no data.

run.description: Present only when `/execute` with `waitSeconds` gave up waiting: the run is still going (or parked), and this is how to follow it. Absent on every answer that finished in the call.

semanticCallLog.description: The actual searches as `producer: mode search on index (k=…)`, in order.

semanticCalls.description: Relevance searches behind a semantic anchor: one embedding plus one similarity scan per anchor. The third call axis — a search of an index is neither a producer fetch nor a reduction, and a semantic query spends here and nowhere else.

warnings.description: Caveats on this result that do not make it an error — a producer that failed, rows that are partial or supporting context, an aggregate over mixed units. Absent when there are none.

KgRefineRequest.description: Cypher to revise and what to change about it — the body of `/refine`.

cypher.description: The current Cypher, possibly hand-edited, that the revision starts from.

instruction.description: What to change, in plain language. Echoed back as the response's `question`.

KgRefreshViewResponse.description: Whether a materialised view's cache was recomputed.

name.description: The view's name, as given in the path.

refreshed.description: False for a regular or unknown view — nothing was recomputed.

KgReprojectResponse.description: How much of a user's stored propositions were re-projected into graph edges.

durationMs.description: Wall-clock time the reprojection took, in milliseconds, from resolving the user to the last edge persisted.

username.description: The user whose propositions were re-projected, echoed from the username parameter.

KgRunConflictResponse.description: The run was not awaiting input; its actual state travels with the refusal.

detail.description: Why it is in that state, when anything was recorded. Null otherwise.

error.description: Always `run is not awaiting input`; `state` says what the run is doing instead.

state.description: The run's real state: RUNNING, COMPLETED, KILLED, FAILED, CANCELLED or EXPIRED.

KgRunRef.description: A watchable run handle. Its presence means the rows are 'not yet', not 'none'.

answer.description: Where to send the owner's pick for a parked run. Absent while running.

choices.description: The `{kind, question, options, context}` payload when parked.

kill.description: Where to stop the run. Absent when parked — nothing is executing to kill.

poll.description: Where to poll for state and, once settled, the result.

KgRunState.description: The state of a background run, with its result once it has settled.

choices.description: The question a parked run poses to its owner.

cypher.description: The Cypher the run executes, as submitted to `/execute` after any parameter substitution.

detail.description: Why the run ended as it did, when anything was recorded.

endedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds at which the run settled. Absent while running or parked.

expiresAt.description: Epoch milliseconds at which a parked run lapses into EXPIRED.

result.description: The query result. Present only when `state` is COMPLETED.

runId.description: The run id from the path, echoed back.

startedAt.description: Epoch milliseconds at which the run started.

state.description: RUNNING, WAITING_INPUT (parked on `choices`), or one of the settled states COMPLETED, KILLED, FAILED, CANCELLED or EXPIRED.

KgSaveViewRejection.description: A view was refused: a bad name, an unrunnable body, or a name already taken.

error.description: Why the view was refused. Always present.

name.description: The requested name, trimmed. Absent when the declaration itself was malformed — a reserved or uncoercible param, say — and refused before a save was attempted.

violations.description: Preflight defects when the body names shapes the schema contradicts.

KgSaveViewRequest.description: A user-authored view to save into the acting user's world: the body of `POST /views`.

cypher.description: The view's body. RETURN one node variable for a view that composes as a label, or a projection for a tabular view run directly. Must pass the schema preflight with declared defaults substituted.

description.description: One line on what the view answers, shown to the query generator beside the schema. Defaults to empty.

materialized.description: Cache the result and serve reads from the cache until `ttl` lapses. Defaults false: a regular view re-runs on every read.

name.description: A plain identifier — letters, digits and underscore, not starting with a digit — because a query uses it as a label. Trimmed before it is checked; a name a shipped view owns is refused.

outputLabel.description: The node label the view's rows are, e.g. `Person`. A materialized view with one caches its member nodes; without one it keeps its rows as a snapshot. A regular view does not need it.

params.description: Bind variables the body references as `$name`, by name. A materialized view may declare none.

ttl.description: Cache lifetime for a materialized view, e.g. `30m`, `2h`, `1d`. Absent means `1h`; ignored for a regular view.

name.description: The name the view was saved under — the requested name, trimmed.

note.description: Why the stored query differs from the one sent

ok.description: Always true; a refusal answers 400 with a different body.

savedCypher.description: The stored query, when promotion inlined captured scopes into it

KgSchemaLabel.description: A node label and its sampled property shape.

anchor.description: True when this label may open a MATCH pattern bare — a real read, or a virtual population implicitly bound by user tenancy. False means it is reachable only by traversal from a bound anchor; an editor should not offer it at first position. Defaults true so an older client reading a newer appliance loses nothing.

description.description: The declared definition of the type this label names, verbatim from the realm's own registry — for an editor to show on hover. Null for core/introspected labels, which declare none.

exhaustive.description: True when every node carrying this label was inspected, so an absent property genuinely does not exist here. False means the sample was capped — evidence of what exists, and no evidence at all about what does not.

label.description: The node label, as a MATCH pattern writes it.

properties.description: The properties seen on the sampled nodes. See `exhaustive` for what an absence means.

realm.description: The realm that declared this label's type. Null means core — the world's own types or the host's.

sampleCount.description: How many nodes were sampled when inferring the properties.

KgSchemaProperty.description: A property observed on nodes carrying a label.

alternateKey.description: True when the realm's type declares this property as an ALTERNATE KEY: it identifies the same record as the identity does, in the vocabulary the source's own readers use. A policy's `policy_identifier` is its identity; its `policy_number` is what a view shows and what a client will try to join on. Both name the same policy. Unlike the identity, an alternate key is not the dedupe key and is not required on write, so a type may declare several. Defaults false.

description.description: The property's DECLARED description, verbatim from the realm's registry — for an editor to show on hover. Null where the declaration documents nothing.

identity.description: True when the realm's type declares this property as the node's IDENTITY. Two columns denote the same thing only when both project the identity of the same label; matching names prove nothing, and a client that joins on them will relate records that are not related. Defaults false so an older client reading a newer appliance loses nothing, and so an undeclared property is never mistaken for a key.

name.description: The property key, as a query writes it after the dot.

sparse.description: True when the property was missing from a non-trivial fraction of the sample.

type.description: Inferred type tag: string, long, datetime, list<string>, any, …

KgSchemaRelationship.description: A (from, type, to) triple observed in the world subgraph.

from.description: The label of the node the relationship starts from.

to.description: The label of the node the relationship points to.

KgSchemaResponse.description: Labels, their properties, and relationship triples reachable by the acting user.

labels.description: Every label in the snapshot, virtual ones included. Empty only when there is no snapshot.

refreshedAt.description: When the snapshot was taken, ISO-8601. Absent when there is no snapshot.

relationships.description: The (from, type, to) triples in the snapshot. Empty only when there is no snapshot.

KgScopeDeleteResponse.description: The outcome of deleting a captured scope.

deleted.description: True when a scope was dropped; false when the user had no live scope of that name, which is not an error.

name.description: The scope name from the path, echoed back.

KgScopeInfo.description: A captured query scope: a frozen result set referenced in a later query as (x:`$name`).

expiresAt.description: When the scope lapses, ISO-8601 — null means PINNED (kept until deleted).

members.description: How many members the capture froze. Membership is frozen; values stay live.

name.description: The name the scope was captured under, unique per user; a later query binds it as (x:`$name`).

outputLabel.description: The node label later references bind with.

statement.description: The statement that produced the capture — the scope's provenance.

KgScopeListResponse.description: The acting user's live captured scopes, newest first.

scopes.description: The live scopes, newest first; an expired scope is absent.

KgUnknownScopeResponse.description: The named scope does not exist in the acting user's world; the ones that do travel with the refusal.

available.description: The scope names this world declares (its focuses).

error.description: Names the scope that was not found.

KgValidationResponse.description: The result of validating cypher against the schema without executing it.

message.description: A single human-readable summary, or null when there is nothing to say.

ok.description: True when the cypher passes the strict preflight — the same check strict execution applies.

violations.description: What the schema contradicts, one entry per defect.

KgValueOverflow.description: A property's value domain that is wider than its declared `max`: how wide, and a sample of its shape.

count.description: How many distinct values exist. Null when the source could not be counted.

max.description: The cap that was exceeded — the property's declared `max`.

sample.description: A few values, to show the SHAPE of the domain. NEVER treat this as the set.

KgViewInvocationResponse.description: The runnable cypher for a saved view invoked with the given arguments.

cypher.description: Run this through `/execute`, so a view uses the same engine as any other query.

name.description: The view's name, as given in the path.

KgViewMatch.description: The saved view a question was routed to instead of generating Cypher.

args.description: The arguments the selector bound from the question, by parameter name.

name.description: The saved view's name, as `GET /views` lists it.

reason.description: The selector's one line on why this view.

Message.description: The agent's answer in a chat completion

content.description: The agent's whole answer. When the turn raised requests still waiting for approval, it ends with a note listing each one, the run that raised it, and a link to decide it.

Model.description: An agent, or the world itself, presented as an OpenAI model

created.description: When the list was made, in Unix epoch seconds; not when the agent was created

id.description: The agent's name, or world for the world itself; send it as model to talk to it

ModelList.description: The world itself and the agents the caller can talk to now, as OpenAI models; answered by GET /openai/v1/models and, holding just that agent, GET /agents/{name}/v1/models

data.description: On /openai/v1: world first, unless the caller's API key is an agent key, then the agents that may be talked to now and that the key, if scoped to some agents, reaches

NewDuty.description: A duty an add-duty change would give the agent

every.description: Six-field cron the duty is checked on; null means checked on demand

holds.description: The view or DERIVE label whose rows are the duty's violations

name.description: Name of the new duty; must not match one the agent already has

text.description: The duty's Always/Never rule, in words

QosSpec.description: An agent's quality of service: the priority its work is paced at, and the models it falls back to when one of its own fails mid-check

fallbacks.description: Fallback model names keyed by LLM role. A check whose models and fallbacks all fail is held as unknown, never as upheld

priority.description: interactive, business (the default) or background. Background work takes half of each source it declares no share for; a conversation is interactive whatever is declared

Receipt.description: One decision the Gatekeeper made about a call that would change something on a run's behalf (acted, held for a person, or refused), or a person's answer to such a request. Chained per owner by hash so an edit shows; returned with its run by GET /agents/{name}/runs/{id}

agent.description: Name of the agent holding the work; null when no agent holds it

agentVersion.description: The holding agent's governing signed version number when the decision was made; null when none governs it

at.description: ISO-8601 instant it was written, to the millisecond

decidedBy.description: Username of the person who approved or rejected; null when the Gatekeeper decided

decision.description: `act` (let through), `request` (held for a person), `refused`, or a person's `approved` or `rejected`

entityKeys.description: Business records the call's arguments name, as `field=value`: a field called `id`, `key`, `number`, `res_id` or `external_id`, or ending `Id`, `_id`, `Key`, `_key`, `Url` or `_url`. At most 20

hash.description: SHA-256 hex over everything else this receipt says, as canonical JSON with keys sorted and times as ISO-8601 text

id.description: The receipt's id, `rc_` and a UUID

inputHash.description: SHA-256 hex of the call's input as sent, or of the empty string when it had none

ownerId.description: Id of the user whose chain the receipt belongs to

previousHash.description: The hash of the receipt before it in the owner's chain; empty for the first

reason.description: Why, in words, up to 500 characters; empty when none was given

requestId.description: Id of the request it raised or answered; null for `act` and `refused`

rule.description: What decided: `authority`, `halted`, `egress`, `observing`, `never` or `review` for the Gatekeeper, `person` for a person's answer; `refused` when a refusal named no rule

runId.description: Id of the run the decision was made for; null for a person's answer to a request that names no run

seq.description: Position in the owner's chain, counting from 1

verb.description: The verb called, as the gateway names it

work.description: Name of the routine the call was made from

RequestMessage.description: One message of an OpenAI chat request's history

content.description: A string, or a list of content parts of which only the {type: text, text} ones are read, joined by newlines; anything else reads as empty

role.description: user or assistant; messages with any other role, such as system, are not read

RetireRequest.description: Why an agent is being retired, sent to POST /agents/{name}/retire

reason.description: The reason, recorded with the retirement after trimming; may be empty

Retired.description: What retiring an agent took with it, as POST /agents/{name}/retire answers: the agent is off duty for good and its record is kept

agent.description: Name of the agent that was retired

keysRevoked.description: How many of your API keys were revoked because they could talk to this agent, including keys scoped to other agents as well

slotsDeleted.description: How many of the agent's own credential slots (its own-account secrets) were deleted from your wallet

RoutineView.description: A routine on an agent's card (AgentView.routines): a TypeScript action or realm-scheduled function, with the stage chosen for it and the stage it actually fires at

description.description: The action's own description; empty when the routine does not exist in this world

firing.description: The stage dispatch actually honours for it (off, observing or on). Lower than `stage` when something the agent still needs holds it back; off for a missing routine

missing.description: True when the agent names a routine that does not exist in this world

name.description: The action's name, as the agent names it

stage.description: The stage chosen for this routine (off, observing or on): a stored override, else its declared stage, else the agent's, before the agent's own standing is applied

trigger.description: What fires it, in words: "when <signal type> arrives", "on schedule <cron>", "on the realm's schedule <cron>", both joined by a comma, "no trigger", or "not found" for a missing routine

RunDetail.description: One run of an agent, with a receipt for every decision made on its behalf; answered by GET /agents/{name}/runs/{id}

receipts.description: Receipts for the decisions the Gatekeeper made during the run, in the order they were made

run.description: The run itself: what started it, its state, timing and output

RunNowRequest.description: One of an agent's scheduled jobs to run now, outside its schedule; sent to POST /agents/{name}/upcoming/run

job.description: Name of the scheduled job, as a firing's job in GET /agents/{name}/upcoming

SecretValue.description: The agent's own value for a secret, sent to PUT /agents/{name}/accounts/{secret}

value.description: The secret value itself, kept as an API key and sent instead of the sponsor's on an own-account API; never returned

SetStageRequest.description: A move on the stage ladder for an agent, or for one routine it holds; sent to POST /agents/{name}/stage

routine.description: Name of one routine the agent holds, to move only that routine; null or absent moves the agent as a whole

stage.description: Stage to move to: off (never fires), observing (runs with writes suppressed) or on (may write). An unrecognised value reads as off

SkipRequest.description: Skip the next scheduled firing of one of an agent's jobs, or postpone it; sent to POST /agents/{name}/upcoming/skip

job.description: Name of the scheduled job, as a firing's job in GET /agents/{name}/upcoming

reason.description: Why, kept with the skip after trimming; may be empty

until.description: When to run the skipped firing instead, ISO-8601 instant in the future; null or absent skips it outright

Slots.description: The secrets an agent keeps its own value for, by name only; answered by the /agents/{name}/accounts endpoints

secrets.description: Names of the secrets the agent has its own value for, as the realm's keys declare them, sorted; the values are never returned

StageResponse.description: The agent after a stage change or signature, or why the change was refused; answered by POST /agents/{name}/stage and POST /agents/{name}/sign

agent.description: The agent after the change; null when it was refused

refused.description: Why the change was refused, in words; null when it was made

StartFillRequest.description: What to fill: the body of POST /admin/kg/fills

budgetPerTick.description: Units of paid work one tick may buy: a producer fetch group or a group of an inline model judgement, not HTTP requests or tokens. Clamped to 1-500; defaults to 60 when absent

cypher.description: The Virtual Cypher query whose materialization the fill drives; every tick re-runs it. Blank is a 400

label.description: Display name for the fill, shown in its activity; empty when absent, and the fill id is shown instead

SweepSpec.description: A sweep: a cold materialization an agent keeps filled by running a saved view pass after pass, under a budget, until a pass buys nothing

budgetPerTick.description: Most units of paid work (a producer fetch, or a group of an inline judgement) one pass may buy; null takes the host's default

name.description: The sweep's name within its agent; part of the fill's identity, so starting it twice is one fill

view.description: Name of a saved view of this world that takes no arguments: the query each pass runs

TipSchedule.description: When a tip is posted to the acting user's inbox, as a frequency preset and an hour; the body of PUT /hints/schedule

frequency.description: How often a tip is posted; NEVER turns tips off. Defaults to WEEKDAYS when absent

hour.description: Hour of day, 0-23, in the user's own time zone. Defaults to 9 when absent; outside 0-23 is a 400

TipScheduleView.description: The acting user's tip schedule and the cron expression it runs on; answered by GET and PUT /hints/schedule

cron.description: Spring six-field cron expression the schedule runs on (second minute hour day month day-of-week), read in the user's own time zone; null when frequency is NEVER

frequency.description: How often a tip is posted to the inbox; NEVER means tips are off

hour.description: Hour of day (0-23) the tip is posted, in the user's own time zone

TourDeletedResponse.description: Whether a saved tour was removed

deleted.description: True when a tour this user saved was removed. False when the tour is not the caller's to remove — a realm's or the world's own — or no deletable tour has that id

yaml.description: The tour's YAML, as exported or as a realm would ship it

TourListResponse.description: Every tour declared for a world

tours.description: The tours, shipped, realm-contributed and user-saved alike; on import, only the tours just stored

TourRefusal.description: Why a tour was refused, in the server's own words

error.description: The refusal, as a sentence to show the user

TourStepStatusRequest.description: The parameters a tour has collected so far, bound into the step's precondition

params.description: Values the tour has collected so far, by name, bound as query parameters of the step's precondition

TourStepStatusResponse.description: Whether a step's precondition is already satisfied

detail.description: Why, when the status is UNKNOWN — the query error in the author's words

status.description: DONE when the step's precondition returned a row, or when its `when` condition returned none (the step does not apply here); TODO when it is not yet satisfied or has no precondition; UNKNOWN when its query could not be run or the tour or step does not exist, in which case the client should run the step anyway

TourStepView.description: One step, as its file declared it — minus the precondition, which stays server-side

presentation.description: Everything the step's YAML declared except its `doneWhen` and `when` preconditions, carried through uninterpreted — the client owns that vocabulary

watchable.description: This step HAS a precondition, without saying what it is. A client that hands a step to the user can then poll for it and carry on by itself when the world says the user has done the thing — go and connect a coding agent, and the tour notices. Without this flag a client would have to poll every hand-over blindly, spending a query every few seconds on steps that can never come true.

TourSummary.description: A tour: its identity, its provenance, and the client's own declarations

declaredId.description: What the tour's own file called it — the id that survives an export

deletable.description: This world can remove it. NOT the same as userSaved: a tour hand-written into a user's own config is theirs but is not this server's to delete, so a client offering Delete for it would offer a button that silently does nothing.

id.description: Unique within this world, and what every other call addresses

presentation.description: Everything the tour's YAML declared beyond id and steps, uninterpreted

source.description: The realm that shipped it, or absent for a world's own and a user's own. Carried rather than derived from the id — a namespace prefix is not something a client can reliably strip.

steps.description: The tour's steps in walking order; a step's position here is the `index` the status call takes

userSaved.description: Imported or recorded by this user, rather than shipped by a realm or the world

Upcoming.description: What an agent will do next: its scheduled firings, the routines that wait for a signal, the requests its last duty checks say to expect, work in flight, and its recent counts. Answered by GET /agents/{name}/upcoming and after a skip or run-now

agent.description: Name of the agent, as asked

counts.description: What it has done lately, in the units a budget is set in

expected.description: Duties whose next check is expected to raise requests again

firings.description: Its scheduled duty checks and routines, soonest first, those with no next time last. Only jobs the scheduler holds: a duty whose agent is off duty has none

inFlight.description: Its runs still in progress, from its 500 most recent

onSignals.description: Names of the routines it holds that have no scheduled job: the ones that run when something happens rather than at a time

UpcomingResponse.description: What an agent will do next after a skip or a run-now, or why the change was refused

refused.description: Why the change was refused, in words; null when it was made

upcoming.description: The agent's upcoming work after the change; null when it was refused

ViewDebugInfo.description: A saved view visible to the acting user — world or realm tier — with its definition and, for a materialised view, its cache state. The items of `GET /views`.

cachedMembers.description: Nodes — or, for a row snapshot, rows — the cache holds. Null for a regular view, or a materialised one with nothing cached.

cypher.description: The view's Cypher body, trimmed, with any `$name` parameter references as declared.

dataContract.description: The ODCS contract the view is pinned to, and in which mode. Absent when it is not contracted.

description.description: One line on what the view answers. Empty when it declares none.

expiresAt.description: Epoch milliseconds at which the cache expires; may already be past. Null for a regular view, or a materialised one with nothing cached.

materialized.description: True when reads are served from a cache that is recomputed once `ttl` lapses.

name.description: The view's name, which a query uses as a label and `/views/{name}` paths take.

outputLabel.description: The node label the view's rows are. Null for a tabular view, and for a materialised view that keeps its rows as a snapshot.

params.description: Declared bind variables by name. Empty for an unparameterized view, and always for a materialised one.

source.description: The realm that shipped the view. Null for a view of the world's own.

ttl.description: Cache lifetime, e.g. `30m`, `2h`, `1d`. Null for a regular view.

ViewParamSpec.description: A declared bind variable of a saved view, referenced as $name in its Cypher and supplied per invocation, keyed by that name wherever a view's params are declared or listed

choices.description: The fixed set of values this param accepts — rendered as a select, enforced at invocation. Absent = any value of the declared type.

default.description: Used when an invocation omits this param. Absent = required on invocation, unless required: false.

description.description: What the argument means — rendered verbatim as the field's hint.

required.description: false lets an invocation omit a param that has no default; it is then bound to null.

type.description: The coercion applied to supplied values, and the form control a UI renders (int/number a number field, boolean a checkbox, date a date picker). float and double are aliases of number.
